chunks: From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi, from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Aban together, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Zoroastrian man who had a wife upon his religion, then he converted to Islam or she converted. He said: Wait for the completion of her waiting period (iddah). If he converts, they remain upon their first marriage. If he does not convert until the waiting period is completed, then she is divorced from him. And that which indicates that as long as he is upon the conditions of the dhimma (non-Muslim subject), she does not divorce from him, even if her waiting period is completed.

key_terms.بِشَرَائِطِ الذِّمَّةِ: Upon the conditions of the dhimma (non-Muslim status)
key_terms.عِدَّتُهَا: Her waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death
key_terms.نِكَاحِهِمَا الْأَوَّلِ: Their first marriage (continuity of the original contract)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a Zoroastrian couple if the husband or wife converts to Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'Iddah (waiting period) for a Zoroastrian woman whose husband remains a dhimmi after her conversion, establishing that the marriage is not automatically dissolved until the Iddah concludes. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the immediate validity of the initial contract upon one spouse's conversion and the conditional dissolution if the other does not follow suit within the prescribed timeframe. This ruling underscores the importance of religious compatibility (din) as a pillar of marital continuity in Islamic jurisprudence.
